knowledge_point.title: Identifying Vector Fields That Satisfy the Unit Curl Property

question.:question/problem:
Let $C$ be a simple, piecewise-smooth, closed, and positively oriented curve. Given that the line integral

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,\text{d}x+Q\,\text{d}y
$$

 
represents the area of the region $D$ enclosed by any such curve in ${R}^{2},$ which of the following could be the functions $P(x,y)$ and $Q(x,y)?$

I. $P(x,y)=-\frac{y}{3}$ and $Q(x,y)=\frac{x}{3}$

II. $P(x,y)=y\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $Q(x,y)=x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x$

III. $P(x,y)={y}^{2}$ and $Q(x,y)={x}^{2}$
question.:question/worked-solution:
According to Green's theorem, if 

$$
\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y}=1,
$$

we can write the area of the region $D$ enclosed by the curve $C$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(D) & ={∬}_{D}\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\text{d}A \\  & ={∮}_{C}P\,\text{d}x+Q\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

  

With that in mind, let's examine each pair in turn.

- Pair I does *not* give the required area. In this case, 
$\frac{∂P}{∂y}=-\frac{1}{3}$
and
$\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=\frac{1}{3},$
which gives

$$
\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y}=\frac{2}{3}\ne 1.
$$

- Pair II gives the required area. Notice that
$\frac{∂P}{∂y}=\operatorname{sin}⁡x$
and
$\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x$
which gives

$$
\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y}=1.
$$

- Pair III does *not* give the required area. Notice that 
$\frac{∂P}{∂y}=2y$
and
$\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=2x,$
which gives

$$
\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y}=2x-2y\ne 1.
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."
